guidelines.detail: same as LRN-005 (The description supports the stated transitions from the start event to the first activity, between logging and assignment-related work, and from notification to reimbursement when approved. These records support preserving the described sequence; LRN-005 already states essentially the same guideline.)

refines PROC-05 (The description permits feedback after resolution, and the generated model omits that stated activity. PROC-05 covers triggers after the main flow, while this guideline clarifies that such follow-up is optional; LRN-008 covers optional activities without specifying their post-completion relationship.)

refines FID-01 (The description says the process begins when the customer files a complaint, while the reference includes a distinct activity between the start event and logging the complaint. The missing flows support preserving that initiating action and its stated order. This refines FID-01 by specifying how to model a concrete action that initiates a process.)

refines FID-03 (The description says the team evaluates the complaint and refund justification and notifies the customer, while the generated task label names only the notification (P4, S3). This refines the general requirement for short, faithful labels in FID-03 by specifying how to label an activity that combines evaluation and communication.)

same as LRN-024 (The description places customer feedback after the case is resolved and says customers can provide it, so it is optional. The records show the feedback activity and its post-resolution placement are absent. This matches learned guideline LRN-024.)

same as LRN-026 (The description includes both determining an outcome and notifying another participant, while the generated task label names only the notification. This is already covered by learned guideline LRN-026.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points: Connect each consecutive activity with a sequence flow, preserving the stated transitions through branches and synchronization points.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents distinct activities or events in an ordered progression, including a transition into a branch

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that participants may perform a follow-up activity after the main outcome has been reached: Model the follow-up activity as optional and post-completion; represent its relationship to the main flow without making it a required step before the main outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that participants may perform a follow-up activity after the main outcome has been reached

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies a concrete action that initiates the process: Model that action as an activity after the start event, and connect it by sequence flow to the next described activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies a concrete action that initiates the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an activity evaluates information and communicates a resulting outcome to another participant: Label the corresponding task to preserve both the evaluation and the communication, rather than naming only the communication.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an activity evaluates information and communicates a resulting outcome to another participant
